resources.string: When an OTP field is focused, temporarily watch notifications for a verification code, then fill that field only after you confirm. This service does not read the SMS inbox, does not write to the clipboard, and does not autofill without your confirmation.
Notification access: on, but the service is not connected
Accessibility: on, but the service is not connected
Watching: on (waiting for an OTP notification)
Watching: standby (no OTP field detected yet)

OTP Fill only reads notifications while an OTP field is focused (or after you start watching manually). When a 4–8 digit code arrives, a half-screen prompt asks whether to fill it. The code is written into the field only after you tap Fill. It is never copied to the clipboard, and the SMS inbox is never read.

Two system permissions are required:
• Notification access: while watching, read the code and a short source name from notifications
• Accessibility: detect the OTP field, show the confirm prompt, and fill the field after you agree
Notification access is used only while watching, to extract a verification code. The SMS inbox is not read, and the confirm prompt never shows the full SMS or email body.
Accessibility is used only to detect OTP fields, show the confirm prompt, and fill the focused field after you tap Fill.

Focusing an OTP field in a webpage or app starts watching notifications. After the keyboard appears or focus is briefly lost, watching continues for about 80 seconds. Leaving the OTP page, waiting out the timeout, or turning the switch off stops it. You can also start watching manually. Incoming codes always ask for confirmation; nothing is filled silently.
This app does not use the network and does not collect analytics. Turn the switch off to stop watching immediately.
This fills the current OTP field only. The code is not copied to the clipboard.
Could not autofill. Please type the code yourself.
